summary:
SELENIS is an interactive 3D Lunar South Pole Navigator developed by Team TIMOREX to support mission planning and public exploration for humanity’s return to the Moon. At the lunar South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at extreme grazing angles of 1.5° to 5°, causing crater rims to cast massive, shifting shadows while Earth oscillates low above the horizon. Moving a lander by just a few hundred meters can mean the difference between near-continuous solar power and weeks of freezing darkness with lost communications.

Built with React, Three.js, and scientific data derived from NASA LROC/LOLA Digital Elevation Models and JPL Horizons ephemerides, SELENIS simulates real-time terrain shadows, 360° lander-perspective horizon obstructions, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) radio line-of-sight, and Earth libration paths. Featuring a dual-mode interface—Planner Mode for technical telemetry and Explorer Mode for intuitive visual storytelling—SELENIS empowers both mission engineers and the general public to evaluate safe, power-rich lunar landing sites.
details:
What Does It Do & How It Works?

SELENIS operates through a decoupled, three-layer architecture engineered for both scientific rigor and zero-backend browser performance:

  1. Offline Scientific Data Pipeline (Python)
    Built with Python 3.13, NumPy, Rasterio, and Pillow, our geospatial pipeline processes NASA LRO LOLA GeoTIFF Digital Elevation Models and NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris queries. It mathematically ray-traces 360° azimuth horizon masks, terrain slopes, hourly solar illumination, and Direct-to-Earth line-of-sight visibility (accounting for local crater rims and Earth’s figure-eight libration), exporting curated JSON telemetry and quantized WebP heightmaps/hillshades.
    • 3D Crater & Hemisphere Views: Seamless switching between a global Southern Hemisphere view and high-resolution local crater terrain (such as Shackleton Connecting Ridge) with interactive custom pin placement and smooth camera focus transitions.
    • 360° Lander POV Horizon Chart: An interactive SVG panorama plotting local crater rim silhouettes against live Sun and Earth azimuth/elevation trajectories to pinpoint exact eclipse and DTE blackout windows.
    • Micro-Shift Delta Comparison: Side-by-side quantitative evaluation of candidate sites (e.g., Site A vs. Site B across ~450–500 m shifts) comparing solar availability percentage, maximum continuous darkness hours, DTE uptime, and slope hazards.
    • Dual Persona Modes (Planner vs. Explorer): Inspired by modular aerospace HUDs, users can toggle between raw technical telemetry (Planner Mode) and visual progress bars with plain-language takeaways (Explorer Mode) to help differentiate between Professional and General Users.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing Planetary Data
    Compresses gigabytes of raw NASA planetary GeoTIFFs and ephemeris tables into a lightweight static web app that runs smoothly in standard browsers without heavy servers or installations.
  • Decision Support & STEM Education
    Helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts intuitively grasp why micro-topography governs power and communications at the lunar poles, while giving technical reviewers transparent access to dataset provenance and resolution limits.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: JavaScript (ES2024), React 18.3, Vite 8, Three.js (0.187), React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), @react-three/drei, custom GLSL shaders, Tailwind CSS v4, and Lucide React.
  • Scientific Data Pipeline: Python 3.13, uv (package & environment manager), NumPy, Rasterio (GeoTIFF DEM processing), and Pillow (WebP texture encoding).
  • Open Space Data Sources: NASA LRO LOLA Digital Elevation Models (DEM), NASA JPL Horizons Ephemeris System, NASA Moon Trek, and ASU/NASA LROC QuickMap.
  • Validation, Testing & DevOps: Node.js 24 native test runner (node --test), Python unittest, custom SHA-256 dataset validator (validate-data.mjs), ESLint 10, Ruff, GitHub Actions CI (multi-OS checks), and Netlify static deployment.
  • UI/UX Prototyping: Figma and Google Stitch.

How Is the Project Creative?

  • Decoupling Scientific Truth from GPU Approximation
    Over multi-kilometer lunar terrain, standard WebGL shadow maps alone can suffer from frustum bias. SELENIS computes mathematically exact horizon ray-tracing in Python while synchronizing 3D directional lighting and interactive pin placement in Three.js for immediate spatial intuition.
  • Zero-Asset Procedural Deep-Space Rendering
    Instead of heavy HDRI environment maps that wash out realistic airless lunar shadow contrast and bloat bundle size, SELENIS renders a custom GLSL procedural galaxy sky dome and multi-layer parallax starfield with zero external texture overhead.
  • Interactive Micro-Shift Discovery
    Allowing users to add or reposition landing markers directly on the 3D terrain turns abstract orbital geometry into a hands-on experiment showing how a few hundred meters dramatically changes mission survivability.

What Factors Did Our Team Consider?

  • Scientific Honesty & Provenance
    Every public dataset asset requires documented source URLs, reference frames, resolution disclaimers, and SHA-256 hashes, paired with an in-app Scientific Data Report that clearly separates measured terrain coverage from unmodeled far-field obstructions.
  • Cross-Device Performance
    We implemented WebGL2 capability detection, adaptive device pixel ratios, quantized WebP textures (enforced under a 10 MiB/file budget), and a serverless architecture so the app maintains responsive frame rates on standard laptops.
  • Multi-Audience Accessibility
    Designing a collapsible HUD and dual Planner/Explorer views ensures the interface is clean and approachable for the general public while preserving exact angular and slope telemetry for technical judges.
